name: Zul'Gurub: Delusions of Jin'do still works after adding its invisibility detection (#9661)
contract: The Shade of Jin'do (14986) casts its own invisibility (24307, SPELL_AURA_MOD_INVISIBILITY type 2).
Vanilla's Delusions of Jin'do (24306) always paired the curse with SPELL_AURA_MOD_INVISIBILITY_DETECT
type 2 as its third (and only aura) effect, so the cursed player could see and fight back the Shade
they are forced to summon. The Ascension replacement curse (2118511/2118512) carried the vision and
the damage but not that detection, so the cursed hero could not see or target the Shade.
boss_jindo_coa.cpp now reuses only that third effect of 24306 on the cursed player, through the real
Delusions trigger (verified by reading the applied aura directly in the fix's own code path).
This harness cannot observe the grant itself: the lane's own isolating phase makes Jin'do lose the
hero and evade within the same window the curse lands (documented independently by the sibling
zul-gurub-jindo-resets-5800 scenario's contract), and 24306's own, unmodified Blizzard
AuraInterruptFlags (bit 31, leave combat) then strips it before any external assertion can observe it
-- confirmed empirically: the vision (2118511) and damage (2118512) halves of the same curse remain
readable afterward, but 24306 reads false at every tried poll width down to 50 ms, immediately after
the curse lands. The Shade (14986) is equally unobservable here: nearby_creature_count never finds
it even on the unmodified tree, independent of this fix. So this scenario only proves the fix did not
break the rest of the Delusions curse (the vision and damage auras, and the fight itself), which would
fail if the added AddAura call threw, deadlocked, or otherwise disrupted the surrounding cast.
No scenario in this harness can assert the detection grant or the Shade's visibility directly.
